newsitem.title: USA: Best actress McDormand makes it a family affair.
newsitem.headline: Best actress McDormand makes it a family affair.

text.p: Frances McDormand took home the best actress Oscar on Monday for her role as a pregnant police chief in "Fargo," joining her husband and brother-in-law in the winner's circle.

In her short and emotional acceptance speech, McDormand gave tribute to her new son Pedro as well as her husband Joel Coen and brother-in-law Ethan Coen, who shared the Oscar for best original screenplay.
McDormand praised "Ethan Coen who helped make an actor of me, his brother Joel who helped make a woman of me, and Pedro McDormand Coen who helped make a mother of me."

McDormand and her husband were in the process of adopting Pedro from Paraguay while they were working on "Fargo," in which McDormand waddles her way through a murder investigation in a small town in Minnesota.
McDormand said she had to wait until after the filming had wrapped before she could meet her adopted son.
McDormand said that making "Fargo" was a much needed distraction from counting the days until she would meet her son-to-be. "It made the wait much better, it gave me something to do," she said.
Joel Coen was also nominated for best director and "Fargo" was nominated for best picture.
The movie was one of the quirkiest independent movies to be nominated in what was dubbed "The year of the Independents."
The movie, set in Minnesota, follows a botched kidnapping which results in a series of killings in the normally quiet town.
McDormand's husband Joel told reporters after receiving his statuette that a large part of the movie's success was due to his wife.
"The movie's popularity had a lot to do with Fran's performance in the movie," he said.

McDormand praised "independent-minded directors" for increasing the number of roles for powerful women in movies and asked that they continue producing the best roles for women and "throw in a few for the men."

McDormand made her screen debut in the Coen brothers first feature film "Blood Simple" in 1984. Since then she has worked in numerous films including "Mississippi Burning" in 1988 for which she won a nomination for best supporting actress.
